name: Moderna Museet
funding: SEK 271M income (2025), state 70%. Sponsors: Bank of America, Bloomberg, PwC, Jung, Patriksson and an unnamed wine and spirits supplier; partners Hotel Skeppsholmen and Panasonic Connect.
watch: Sponsor Bloomberg: more than 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg Philanthropies in May 2026. Moderna Museet was not named.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2015 to 2025 with accounts, names sponsors and partners on its support page, and lists its Board of Trustees.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Australia (MCA)
funding: AUD 28M. Australia Council for the Arts, NSW Government, Telstra, Qantas, private benefactors.
watch: Major Sydney harbourfront museum with prominent Australian corporate sponsors.

name: Kunstmuseum Den Haag
funding: Gemeente Den Haag owns the collection and subsidises the museum. VriendenLoterij gives €500,000 a year. Mondriaan Fonds, Vereniging Rembrandt, Aronson Antiquairs and several funds also give.
watch: Governed under the Dutch Cultural Governance Code.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2017 to 2025 with a balance sheet and income statement, names its funders each year, and lists the supervisory board.

name: De Pont
funding: Private museum run by a foundation built on the estate of Jan de Pont.
watch: Established in 1992 by the bequest of jurist and entrepreneur Jan de Pont.
records_note: Its site states the foundation is self-funded and audited, posts a two-year income summary only, lists a five-member board, and names no funders or reports.

name: Mori Art Museum
funding: Corporate endowment from Mori Building Co., Shiseido, corporate sponsors.
watch: Real-estate developer cultural initiative with luxury and financial corporate circle.

name: The Power Plant Contemporary Art Gallery
funding: Registered charity The Art Gallery at Harbourfront. Canada Council, Ontario Arts Council and Toronto Arts Council; BMO Financial Group sponsors free admission.
watch: BMO Capital Markets managing director Katrina Rempel sits on the board. RBC, named earlier, is not on the current page.
records_note: Posts 14 annual reports from 2012-13 to 2025-26 naming supporters, and lists its board, but the latest shows only a draft statement of operations.

name: Le Fresnoy - Studio national des arts contemporains
funding: €5.2M. Ministère de la Culture, Région Hauts-de-France, Métropole Européenne de Lille.

name: Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo
funding: Private foundation of Patrizia Sandretto Re Rebaudengo; family links to Asja Energy (renewables).
records_note: FSRR posts a yearly social report with accounts for 2021 to 2025, names its board, and names four partners on an undated page.

name: Contemporary Art Gallery (CAG)
funding: Canada Council, BC Arts Council, BC Gaming Policy and Enforcement Branch, City of Vancouver and Connor, Clark and Lunn Investment Management.
watch: The BC gaming grant is public gambling-proceeds money, which the map grades as an ordinary public funder.
records_note: Lists its board and shows a few undated funder logos; links no annual reports, financial statements or named donor list.

name: Venice Biennale
funding: 2024 budget: public funds EUR 33.1M; tickets, sales and sponsorship 31.4M. 2026 donors include Getty, Ford, Batia and Idan Ofer and the Helis Foundation; Bvlgari and illycaffè are lead sponsors.
watch: The Helis Foundation, a 2026 donor, is funded by the Helis oil family. The EU ended a EUR 2M grant over Russia's pavilion in July 2026. In 2026 the jury resigned, artists withdrew from the awards and pavilions closed for a day.
why_flagged: 2024 budget: public funds EUR 33.1M; tickets, sales and sponsorship 31.4M. 2026 donors include Getty, Ford, Batia and Idan Ofer and the Helis Foundation; Bvlgari and illycaffè are lead sponsors.
records_note: It posts audited accounts for 2020 to 2025, names its board and auditors, and lists 2026 donors by name, but no separate annual report.

name: Château de Versailles
funding: French state public establishment. Dior, The American Friends of Versailles and the Société des Amis de Versailles funded the Salon de Diane ceiling, reopened June 2026.
watch: Dior's parent LVMH drew €518M of tax relief for its Paris foundation, criticised by the Cour des comptes in 2018. Epstein links here are venue-only. See the Epstein cross-reference.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2003 to 2024 and names its board; shows no donor roster, since donors are engraved in the Château and credited per project.
other_findings: Epstein link · Thomas Pritzker · documented: In September 2018 Epstein emailed Jack Lang and his daughter Caroline about a venue for the 2019 Pritzker Architecture Prize ceremony, writing that Pritzker wanted "something unique this time". The ceremony was held at the Palace of Versailles in May 2019; nothing shows Epstein arranged it. Pritzker, whose family runs the prize, kept writing to Epstein after his 2008 conviction and has said he "exercised terrible judgment in maintaining contact". Pritzker stepped down as Hyatt executive chairman on 16 February 2026.

name: Albertina
funding: Annual partners Bank Austria and Verbund; partners BMW and Do&Co. The page says partners are capped at three but shows four logos.
watch: Federal museum of Austria. Self-funding ratio exceeds 60% through strong international tourism; corporate sponsors (Pomerche, UniCredit Bank Austria) comply with Austrian federal transparency mandates.
records_note: Posts business reports from 2018, audited accounts for 2024 and its Kuratorium; sponsors and partners appear as undated logos.
